metadata.processing_notes: Comprehensive knowledge graph extraction from Colonial Office List 1897. Extracted from 39 colony/territory files containing detailed administrative, geographic, economic, demographic, and prosopographic data. All data extracted exactly as written in source documents, preserving historical spelling and terminology.

places.name: Antigua
places.description: Island about 54 miles in circumference, about half the size of Middlesex

places.name: Barbuda
places.description: Dependency of Antigua, lying about 25 miles due north of the main island, very flat, with a large lagoon on the west side, separated from the sea by a spit of sand. Once owned by the Codrington family. Produces salt and phosphates of lime, well adapted for cattle grazing

places.name: Redonda
places.description: Dependency of Antigua, lying between Montserrat and Nevis, 25 miles S.W. of Antigua, 1 mile by 1/4 mile, 1,000 feet high, valuable for phosphate of alumina mines discovered 1865

places.name: St. John
places.description: Chief town of Antigua, port of registry

places.name: Bahamas
places.description: Chain of coral islands, most northerly of the British West Indian Colonies, composed of about 20 inhabited islands and an immense number of islets and rocks, about half the size of Wales

places.name: New Providence
places.description: Principal island containing the capital, Nassau

places.name: Nassau
places.description: Capital of Bahamas, port of registry

places.name: Barbados
places.description: Most easterly of the Caribbean Islands, nearly 21 miles long by 14 in breadth, contains 106,470 acres, a little larger than Rutland

places.name: Bridgetown
places.description: Chief town and port of Barbados, situated in parish of St. Michael, port of registry

places.name: Speightstown
places.description: Only other town besides Bridgetown, has about 1,500 inhabitants

places.name: Carlisle Bay
places.description: Harbour of Barbados, an open roadstead much exposed to wind from south and south-west, has inner harbour or careenage protected by structure called the Mole Head

places.name: Cape of Good Hope
places.description: Colony with Transkei, over five times the size of England, bounded by Atlantic and Southern (Indian) Oceans on west and south, Orange River on north, Orange Free State and Natal on north-west, and Pondoland on east

places.name: Cape Town
places.description: Capital and principal city, port of registry

places.name: Kimberley
places.description: Centre of the Diamond Fields, 647 miles from Capetown and 485 from Port Elizabeth

places.name: Port Elizabeth
places.description: Port of registry, 340 miles from De Aar junction

places.name: East London
places.description: Port and city, port of registry

places.name: Ceylon
places.description: Island in Indian Ocean off southern extremity of Hindustan, ancient Taprobane, extreme length from Point Palmyra to Dondra Head is 266 miles, greatest width 140.5 miles, about equal to Holland and Belgium

places.name: Colombo
places.description: Capital and principal port

places.name: Kandy
places.description: City at 1,865 feet above sea level

places.name: Hong Kong
places.description: Island off south-eastern coast of China at mouth of Canton River, about 40 miles east of Macao, 91 miles south of Canton, irregular ridge with broken peaks rising to nearly 2,000 feet, a third larger than Guernsey

places.name: Kowloon
places.description: Peninsula ceded to Great Britain by Treaty 1861, forms part of the Colony

places.name: Victoria
places.description: City of Hong Kong, extends for four miles at base of hills protecting south side of harbour, contains with suburbs more than 200,000 inhabitants

places.name: Jamaica
places.description: Island in Caribbean Sea south of eastern extremity of Cuba, largest of British West Indies, 144 miles in length, 50 in extreme breadth, about half the size of Wales, very mountainous

places.name: Kingston
places.description: Capital of Jamaica, situated on south coast, port of registry, fine harbour

places.name: Blue Mountains
places.description: Famous mountain range in east of Jamaica, highest peak 7,400 ft. high

places.name: Grand Cayman
places.description: Largest of Cayman Islands, dependency of Jamaica, between 19° 10' and 19° 45' N lat. and 79° 30' and 80° 35' W long., contains about 2,000 inhabitants engaged in catching turtle for export

places.name: Mauritius
places.description: Island in Indian Ocean, nearly equal to Surrey, extreme length 36 miles from north to south, extreme breadth 28 miles from east to west, volcanic formation, surrounded by coral reefs

places.name: Port Louis
places.description: Capital and seat of Government, contains with suburbs 57,367 souls, one of the best harbours in the East, possesses three graving docks, defended by Fort Adelaide and Fort George

places.name: Trinidad
places.description: Island about 16 miles eastward of Venezuela, average length 48 miles, average breadth 35 miles, separated from continent by Gulf of Paria

places.name: Port of Spain
places.description: Chief town and principal port, situated near north-east angle of Gulf of Paria, port of registry

places.name: San Fernando
places.description: Second town and port, about 30 miles south of Port of Spain

places.name: Singapore
places.description: Island at southern extremity of Malayan Peninsula, greatest length about 27 miles by 14 wide, separated from mainland by narrow strait about three-quarters of a mile width, seat of government

places.name: Straits Settlements
places.description: Colony comprising Singapore, Penang, and Malacca, nearly equal to Kent, transferred from Indian Government to Secretary of State for Colonies 1st April 1867

places.name: Penang
places.description: Island about 15 miles long and 9 broad, situated off west coast of Malayan Peninsula at northern extremity of entrance to Straits of Malacca

places.name: Malacca
places.description: Strip of territory on western coast of peninsula between Singapore and Penang, about 110 miles from former and 240 from latter, about 42 miles in length, from 8 to 25 miles in breadth

places.name: Newfoundland
places.description: Island on north-east side of Gulf of Lawrence, greatest length from north to south 350 miles, average breadth about 150, one-third of that of United Kingdom

places.name: Labrador
places.description: Territory from Cape Chilley (Hudson Strait) to Blanc Sablon (Strait of Belle Isle), including basin of Hamilton, included in colony by Letters Patent 28th March 1876, equal to that of United Kingdom, with coastline of some 600 miles

places.name: St. John's
places.description: Capital of Newfoundland

places.name: Cyprus
places.description: Island in eastern basin of Mediterranean Sea, with Asia Minor to north and Syria to east, equal to Kent, Sussex, and Middlesex combined, largest island in Mediterranean except Sicily and Sardinia, greatest length 140 miles, greatest breadth 60 miles

places.name: Nicosia
places.description: City in Cyprus

places.name: Larnaca
places.description: Port on southern coast, 258 miles from Port Said and 1,117 miles from Valletta

places.name: Lagos
places.description: Colony and Protectorate situated on Bight of Benin, Lagos Island is 3.5 square miles, whole Colony and Protectorate probably includes about 1,500 square miles, port is 4,279 miles from Liverpool

places.name: Lagos Island
places.description: Capital of the Colony

places.name: St. Helena
places.description: Island in South Atlantic Ocean, 800 miles S.E. of Ascension, 1,300 from coast of Africa, 10.5 miles long and 3.5 wide, about 30,000 acres, a little larger than Jersey, 4,477 miles from Southampton and 1,695 miles from Cape Town

places.name: Jamestown
places.description: Capital and only town of St. Helena, N.W. of the island

24 members of which Colonial Secretary, Attorney-General, Auditor-General, and Treasurer are ex officio members; 8 members nominated by the Crown and 12 elected members
Representative Assembly of 29 members elected for 14 districts
The Governor, The Officer Commanding the Troops (Major-General R. Fowler Butler), The Colonial Secretary, The Attorney-General, Hon. Sir G. C. Pile M.L.C., Hon. A. J. Pile C.M.G. M.C.P.
Hon. Sir Geo. C. Pile (President) and 6 other members
Elected annually (1894-95), Hon. A. J. Pile C.M.G. as Speaker

institutions.name: Redonda Phosphate Company
institutions.function: Works phosphate of alumina mines under license at 6d. per ton royalty, employs 90 men, exports on average 7,000 tons annually to United States

institutions.name: Colonial Bank
institutions.function: Only bank doing business in Barbados, capital paid up 600,000£ sterling, 13 branches throughout West Indies, deposits about 2,000,000£, note circulation (five dollar notes) of 400,000£, estimated circulation in Barbados 50,000£

institutions.name: University of the Cape of Good Hope
institutions.function: Authority to confer degrees of B.A., M.A., LL.B., D.M.R., M.D. recognized by Letters Patent dated 8th July 1877; also authorized to confer Lit.D., B.Sc., M.Sc., D.Sc., Bachelor of Arts, Master of Music, Doctor of Music by Act No. 6 of 1896

economic_data.notes: Public Debt including 35,000l. borrowed in connection with late Public Bank and 30,000l. Telegraph Cable Loan

infrastructure.name: Barbados Railway
infrastructure.notes: From Bridgetown to parish of Saint Andrew, commenced 1880, completed 10th September 1882, belongs to Barbados Railway Company Limited, receives Government subsidy of 6,000£

infrastructure.name: Police Stations Telephone Line
infrastructure.notes: Telephonic communication between police stations, open to public use

infrastructure.name: Cape Government Railways - Western System
infrastructure.notes: Total mileage open December 1894: 2,253 miles. Three separate systems: Western (starting Cape Town), Midland (starting Port Elizabeth), Eastern (starting East London), connected at De Aar junction

infrastructure.name: Cape Telegraph System
infrastructure.notes: Telegraph wire erected by Government, also 578 miles of telephone wire

infrastructure.name: Ceylon Government Railways
infrastructure.notes: All owned and worked by Government, includes lines: Colombo to Kandy (74.5 miles), Kandy-Matale (17.75 miles), Peradeniya Junction to Bunderawela (91.25 miles), and others

infrastructure.name: Colombo Harbour
infrastructure.notes: South-West Breakwater commenced 1875 completed 1885, 4,200 feet long. Northern Arm, North-West Breakwater and reclamation of 26 acres commenced May 1894. Total expenditure from 1873 to 31st December 1895

infrastructure.name: Jamaica Railway
infrastructure.notes: Kingston to Montego Bay (113 miles), Ewarton branch from Spanish Town (17 miles), Port Antonio branch from Bogwalk (54 miles). Recently purchased by American syndicate

infrastructure.name: Jamaica Internal Telegraph
infrastructure.notes: Line connecting all principal towns with 66 stations

infrastructure.name: Mauritius Government Railways
infrastructure.notes: Four lines all owned and worked by Government: North line Port Louis to Grand River (31 miles), Midland line Port Louis to Mahebourg (36 miles), Moka Flacq line (27 miles), Savanne branch (11 miles)

infrastructure.name: Trinidad Government Railways
infrastructure.notes: Port of Spain to Arima (16 miles) opened 1876, Coppermine line (24.5 miles) opened 1881, extension to Caroni Bay, San Fernando, Princes Town and further extensions under construction. All constructed and paid for by Government

infrastructure.name: Trinidad Internal Telegraph
infrastructure.notes: Constructed by Government, direct telegraphic communication with British Guiana, Grenada, and Saint Croix

infrastructure.name: Newfoundland Railway
infrastructure.notes: St. John's to Harbour Grace, constructed and worked by private company. Branch to Placentia (25 miles) built by Government at cost of $25,000. Railway to Exploits River (200 miles) complete at cost of $3,120,000

infrastructure.name: Newfoundland Telegraph
infrastructure.notes: 2,200 miles of telegraph open, cables start for Europe at Heart's Content and for America at Placentia

demographics.notes: Estimated population, chiefly composed of English, Germans, French, Spanish, and large proportion of East Indians
About 33,000 inhabitants, largest town on whole West African coast

events.description: Antigua discovered by Columbus in 1493, named after a church in Seville called Santa Maria La Antigua
First inhabited by a few English from St. Kitts in 1632
Charles II made formal grant of island to Lord Willoughby, who sent out large number of colonists
Declared a British possession by Treaty of Breda after interval of French occupation
Phosphate of alumina mines discovered in Redonda in 1865
St. Salvador (Guanahani), one of islands composing Bahamas chain, was first land discovered by Columbus on his voyage in 1492
Included in charter given by Queen Elizabeth to Sir Humphrey Gilbert
Settlers from Bermudas found their way in considerable numbers to Eleuthera
New Providence and all islands between 22° and 27° N lat. granted by Charles II to proprietary body
Great Britain confirmed in possession of Bahamas at Peace of Versailles
Exact date of discovery uncertain, said to have been first visited by Portuguese who found it uninhabited, named Las Barbadas after bearded fig-trees
Nominally taken possession of by English ship 'Olive' when almost deserted
Sir William Courteen fitted out two ships, one arrived at Barbados with thirty persons who landed on north side, formed town called St. Peter's Town
Sixty-four settlers commenced erection of wooden houses, threw bridge across river, laid foundation of Bridgetown
Bartholomew de Diaz, Portuguese commander, landed in Algoa Bay
J. A. Van Riebeck, commissioned by Chamber of Seventeen at Amsterdam, landed at Table Bay with 100 persons, took possession on behalf of Dutch East India Company
British force proceeded to Cape to secure it against French for Prince of Orange, Governor refused, capitulation arranged
By Peace of Amiens Cape restored to Batavian Republic and evacuated
Captured again by British Force
At General Peace of 1814 ceded in perpetuity to British Crown
Portuguese formed settlements on west and south of island
Portuguese dispossessed by Dutch
British took possession of Dutch settlements in island, then annexed to Presidency of Madras
Ceylon constituted a separate Colony
War declared against native Government of interior, last Kandyan King taken prisoner, whole island fell under British rule
Colony ceded to Great Britain, then a desolate island sparsely inhabited by fishermen
Cession confirmed by Treaty of Nankin
Charter bears date
Peninsula of Kowloon ceded to Great Britain by Treaty entered into by Lord Elgin with Government of China
Island discovered by Columbus, called it St. Jago after patron saint of Spain, but new name dropped in favour of native one Jamaica (Haymaca - well watered)
First settlement effected on shores of St. Ann's Bay by Esquimel under direction of Diego son of Columbus while Governor of Hispaniola
Attacked by force sent by Cromwell under Admirals Penn and Venables against Hispaniola, capitulated after trifling resistance
Peace made with Spain, title of England to Jamaica recognized by Treaty of Madrid
Port Royal engulfed in great earthquake
Island discovered by Portuguese
First people to occupy it in numbers were Dutch, commander Admiral J. C. Van Neck named it Mauritius in honour of Stadtholder Prince Maurice of Nassau
Few Frenchmen landed, formally took possession on behalf of French East India Company in 1717, later in 1767 on behalf of King of France, name changed to Isle of France
British operation for its capture effected, laws, religion, and customs of inhabitants guaranteed in instrument of capitulation, former name Mauritius restored
Possession of island confirmed to England by Treaty of Paris
Terrible hurricane visited island causing enormous destruction of buildings and crops
Part of town of Port Louis entirely destroyed by fire
During violent cyclone, railway train blown down ravine at Pailles Bridge, five persons killed, great loss of material sustained
Trinidad first discovered by Columbus on his third voyage, taken possession of for Crown of Spain
British expedition sailed from Martinique for reduction of Trinidad, articles of capitulation signed by Sir R. Abercrombie, Admiral Harvey, and Chacon the Spanish governor
Finally ceded to Crown of Great Britain by Treaty of Amiens
Island taken possession of by Stamford Raffles by virtue of treaty with Johor princes, scarcely inhabited until then
Penang (Prince of Wales Island) first British settlement on Malayan Peninsula, ceded to English by Raja of Kedah with proviso that 6,000 dols. be annually paid
Island discovered by John Cabot
Peace of Utrecht, subsequently confirmed by Treaty of Paris, exclusive sovereignty of Newfoundland acknowledged to belong to Great Britain

Convention signed at Constantinople between representatives of Britannic Majesty and Sultan of Turkey, England engaged to join Sultan in resisting Asiatic possessions against Russia, Sultan consented to cede Island of Cyprus to be occupied and administered by England
King Docemo induced to cede his possessions to British Crown in consideration of pension of £1,000 a-year
Territories erected into separate government by Letters Patent
St. Helena discovered by Portuguese Captain Juan de Nova Castella on St. Helena's day, then uninhabited
Taken possession of by East India Company, charter for its administration granted in 1661
Passed from East India Company to direct government of the Colony by Act of Parliament of 1833
